📚 Today you learned

52-Week High/Low as a Technical Reference Point

A 52-week high/low isn't a magic level — it's a memory marker. Every trader watching the tape can see it on the same chart, so it becomes a self-fulfilling reference: longs get nervous near a new low, shorts get aggressive, and stops cluster just below it because that's where "the thesis is clearly broken" for the most people at once. That's exactly SPXC's setup tonight — it printed a fresh 52-week low ($178.88) this week, and your stop ($186.90) sat just above the prior 13-week low, the same kind of memory level. When a stock takes out a well-watched low on decent volume despite good fundamental news (SPXC's $410M FIS Water deal), that's usually not noise — it's the market pricing something you don't have yet, or a purely technical flush through a level everyone was watching. Either way, once it's broken, the level's job is done; don't anchor to it hoping for a bounce back above.

Also today: Bearish divergence — when price makes a new low (or high) but the news/fundamentals point the other way; usually resolves in favor of price, not the news.
